title: split-plane output read plane sizes derived from the stream geometry, not the packet
object: pkt->data, one packet allocation of pkt->size plus padding
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a read length derived from the declared geometry rather than from the buffer it reads
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, no inner layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavformat/img2enc.c carries `if (ysize + 2*usize + (desc->nb_components > 3) * ysize > pkt->size)` before the writes. That guard is absent at ca1c1f29ce47^.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x10230c, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_read_probe_u8 0x1022fc` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions. Capstone measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-capstone/): spatial CAUGHT, sublet CAUGHT. capstone-subobject measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-capstone-subobject/): CAUGHT. cheribsd-subobject measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-cheribsd-subobject/): CAUGHT.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_malloc / av_mallocz / av_calloc / av_malloc_array -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool or AVRefStructPool between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: three successive reads at computed offsets share one buffer, so the crossing is the SUM overrunning rather than any single length being wrong -- which is why the fix's guard adds the three together, including a fourth plane term that only applies when there are more than three components.
